KZN POLITICAL KILLINGS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
People are being gunned down in KZN – the motive is believed to be political – but is it that clear cut?

Unique Selling Point:
PEOPLE ARE BEING KILLED IN KZN – THE MOTIVE IS SAID TO BE POLITICAL. IT’S A STORY THAT WE HAVE NOT COVERED, BUT IT’S NOT GOING AWAY.

IT’S CONTROVERSIAL BECAUSE OF DIFFERENT VIEWS ABOUT WHAT THE REAL REASON IS BEHIND THE APPARENT KILLING SPREE.


Summary:
Political killings in KZN have intensified within the alliance during the post-Polokwane period.

Same the there is a sinister third force at play while other point to an internal struggle for power, positions and access to resources.

The death toll differs according to different soures. We ask what exactly is a political murder? And what is being done to stop this violent trend?


Further information:
THE STATUS QUO
It appears that there is a glaring lack of political will to find out, exactly, who is being killed for political purposes, and how to prevent this from happening again. Political murders need, by their nature, political intervention. They are, after all, not so much capital crimes as they are indicators that something is deeply dysfunctional in our politics. But despite the highly-publicised task teams, there is no indication that they are being treated as anything else but ordinary crimes.

THE TASK TEAMS THAT HAVE YET TO DELIVER
Before the 2016 Local Government Elections, there was a spate of murders. So many, in fact, that the KZN provincial ANC called for a special task team to investigate them. The Hawks had already formulated a task team to deal with political murders, and the national ANC had called for an internal investigation into why the victims were, almost exclusively, ANC members. In fact, as far back as 2011, Police Commissioner Bheki Cele had established an SAPS task team. But none of these four so-called task teams have actually come up with any results, other than ordinary policing.

THE MOERANE COMMISSION OF INQUIRY
KZN Premier Willies Mchunu established the commission in October 2016, chaired by advocate Marumo Moerane, to investigate the high number of political killings in the province since 2011. The hearings are currently under way.

ANC VIEWS
The ANC in KwaZulu-Natal believes the killing of its public representatives could be the result of “sponsored violence” similar to that experienced in the 1980s.

ANC provincial secretary Super Zuma said the violence could be meant to use KwaZulu-Natal as an “entry point” towards destabilising the country.

Zuma said the ANC was not conclusively saying there is a third force element at work, but wants that aspect to be investigated. He said with the recent killings there were patterns which mirrored those of the violence of the 1980s. “It is not just violence, these are assassinations by well trained people,” he said.

JULY 2017: spokesperson for the ANC in KwaZulu-Natal, Mdumiseni Ntuli, has dismissed claims that the recent killings are politically motivated.

The ANC’s Ntuli said: “We cannot confirm that the violence is politically motivated and I urge people to stay away from these baseless assumptions. This issue is not that straightforward. There is no clear political motivation. Therefore, to say that the incident is politically motivated is a very dangerous assumption.”


CRITICISM FROM WITHIN THE ANC RANKS

Former KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu says the organisation must take responsibility for its contribution to the killings in the province & the ANC will need strong leadership that does not rely on factions to survive.

Mchunu said the reason corruption had become so rampant in both the public and the private sector was due to the lack of principled individuals.

"You can’t just be corrupt in an island [sic]. You need people to assist you, you co-opt them, then you become the chief corruptor, they become assistant corruptors." He says corruption within the ANC is partly to blame for the divisions plaguing the party.

"Jellyfish who feel bound to support a corrupt person or corrupt individuals and they become one club. So people get divided not because there is hatred among them, but just because you are defending that side and defending this thing that we should not be defending."

He’s warned corruption factionalism and the manipulation of party lists has put the ANC at the centre of political killings.

Mchunu says corruption breeds hatred within the organisation and warned that the manipulation of ANC processes has contributed to the increase in political murders in the province.
Mchunu says weak internal ANC systems and corruption have linked the party to political murders. “People are always going to compete but make it clean so that competing for positions via manipulation doesn’t yield benefits for anyone.”

VIOLENCE MONITORS VIEWS
Violence monitor Mary De Haas
She said most killings in the province are linked to factions and power struggles in the ANC. “The worst problem is a lack of political will to investigate these murders,” says violence monitor Mary de Haas. “There is no lack of people willing to testify, but no one is joining the dots. And no one is asking the hard questions about where the ultimate culpability lies.”

She might be a better bet – long history violence monitoring – can give interesting comparitive views and experienced insights.

INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES
Lizette Lancaster, a researcher, said political killings could not be looked at in isolation from how SA has generally dealt with conflict.

“There is clearly a culture among some people to get rid of opponents, often for political reasons. All our research shows that in terms of just general political violence there are often hotspots, a type of modus operandi, whether it is political conflict, strike action or vigilantism,” she said.

Looking at the political killings in KZN, Lancaster said with good crime intelligence it was difficult to comprehend how the role players are not known by law enforcement.

WHAT IS BEING DONE?

POLICE
Police Minister Fikile Mbalula said he was beefing up the extraordinary measures already put in place to deal with the violence.

An integrated provincial project task team consisting of the Hawks, the detective service, crime intelligence, the local criminal records centre and the National Prosecuting Authority was announced by Mbalula in May to deal with political killings. Members of the Public Order Policing Unit, the Tactical Response Team, the National Intervention Unit and Visible Policing were also deployed in some of the hotspots.

Despite this, the killings have continued.

The task team investigating political murders in the province has registered 42 cases, 24 of which are murder cases. Almost 35 suspects have been arrested in 10 murder cases, he said.
According to Mulaudzi, almost 24 cases are still under investigation and 28 firearms have been seized.

In September, the Hawks have offered a R450,000 reward for any information that could lead to the arrest of suspects in the ongoing political killings in KwaZulu-Natal.

CRITICISM FOR THE POLICE
Former KZN premier Mchunu says the use of state security organs for political ends is a betrayal of what they fought against during apartheid. Mchunu says there's an urgent need to restore confidence in the police.

“Failure to arrest, it scarps confidence, that’s the consequence, that is where we might be heading if nothing is done to actually make police fire on all engines to ensure necessary confidence in the police, and everybody’s confidence.”

Violence monitor Vanessa Burger (VERY CONTROVERSIAL IN KZN) she accused IPID of having failed to investigate allegations of police misconduct and brutality at Glebelands Hostel in Umlazi. IPID responded asking her sto substantiate claims – back & forth … would rather avoid her.

WHAT IS A POLITICAL MURDER?
Press define a political murder as a killing where the victim had been a political office-bearer, or the motive was linked to their political affiliation. This was far too superficial.

While there were murders where the victim had clearly been blocking someone’s political path. Most of the murders appeared to be business deals gone sour, whistle-blowers getting removed, an overspill from taxi wars, family feuds, revenge killings, thieves falling out, personal disputes and in some cases the wrong person was killed by mistake.

DEATH TOLL
The figure is debatable…. Some say 60 people were gunned down in suspected political assassinations in KwaZulu-Natal between April 2014 and August 2016.

In June, on an official visit to KwaZulu-Natal last month, police minister Fikile Mbalula said that 33 political killings that had taken place in the province since January 2016 were being investigated.

RECENT CASES:

JULY 2017:
Former ANC Youth League secretary general Sindiso Magaqa, now a councillor, and two other ward councillors, Nontsikelelo Mafa and Jabu Mzizi, were attacked by unknown gunmen. All three are in hospital in critical condition. This attack follows three murders in Umzimkhulu this year. Khaya Thobela, the ANC’s regional deputy secretary and Umzimkhulu’s municipal speaker, died after being shot in April. Khayelihle Mgcwaba, a former ward councillor and a political activist, was murdered in mid-May. A few weeks later, Mduduzi Tshivase, a councillor in Harry Gwala district, was gunned down.

MOST RECENT MURDER
30 / 31 AUGUST 2017
African National Congress (ANC) ward 3 councillor Kwazi Mkhize, 34, of the uMkhambathini Local Municipality in the Midlands, was gunned down by an unknown assailant outside the Nkanyezini Community Hall.

He had concluded an extended branch executive committee meeting, where he was reporting on development projects in his ward. According to the ANC in KZN, Mkhize and his siblings were allegedly closing the gate of the community hall when he was killed. "Although details regarding Cde Mkhize’s murder remain sketchy, it appears his attacker fired from behind and killed him on the scene."

RESEARCH
Jouranlist Niki Moore compliped a list of “political murders” over the last 18 months, arranged according to the apparent picture of motive for The Daily Maverick. See has doen extensive research showing that there are overlaps and contradictions, but one thing is clear: the endgame is all about power and money.

INTERVIEWS
NOT QUITE SURE IF WE INTERVIEW INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES - THEY ARE ALWAYS MORE NEUTRAL _ BUT NOT REALLY PRESENT IN KZN.
ALSO NOT SURE ABOUT CASE STUDIES - DO WE INTERVIEW THE FAMILY OF SOMEONE THAT WAS KILLED RECENTLY?
I LIKE THE IDEA OF THE JOURNALIST NIKI MOORE - JUST BECAUSE SHE HAS TAKEN A CRITICAL LOOK AT A NUMBER OF THE MURDERS

Press Release:


KZN Killing Fields
Over the past few months, several people have been brutally gunned down in Kwazulu-Natal. At
face value, the motives seem to be purely political, but is it that clear cut? Experts believe
corruption, dodgy business deals and power struggles may well be behind some of the
killings. Carte Blanche investigates

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: The province of KwaZulu Natal has been plagued by a wave of targeted assassinations believed to be political killings.

More than 30 KZN ANC comrades have been murdered in just under two years across the province.
LINK: The death toll is debatable. So are the motives. But what is fact is that people are being gunned down – people within the ANC. Is it a factionalism, a struggle for power or just corruption…
VO: Politics and corruption go hand in hand – it’s a global trend says Political Analyst, Protas Madlala.

PROTAS: You’ve never heard of someone being killed because that person was for corruption – it is always these people question, who are concerned about the looting of state resources or the monopoly of the access of state resources.

VO: Violence Monitor Mary de Haas has been active in KZN since the eighties - she says the political dynamics in the province have changed - giving rise to political opportunism.

MARY: What we have seen is deterioration of governance, an increase in corruption // together with corruption goes political competition over positions

LINK: Being a mayor or a councillor is something many people would strive – but it’s become a dangerous job – one that some willing to literally kill for.

PROTAS: It’s very easy to become a councillor you don’t need any formal qualification, you need to be a brave person, toy-toying and you buy a few members, local members to push up your name//the deal is once you are a councillor make sure those tenders come my ways – and anyone that stands in the way will have to be removed to the barrel of the gun

VO: ANC KZN Provincial Spokesperson Mdumiseni Ntuli has a more sinister theory.

NTULI: is it not part of what could be the attributes of a coordinated third force, who’s work is probably to disorganise us on a local government level and maybe even having the intentions of destabilising the provincial government.

PROTAS: I don’t buy that crap. // we knew the third force in the 80s – the killings were state sponsored. Here – who is the third force? //if you know who the third force is go tell and the police.

MAC: How is this different from what we saw 90s?
MARY: The violence was widespread // it was not discriminatory – people were caught up in it because they lived in the wrong area – this is different – this is specifically targeting certain people for reasons // which may or may not be political and that makes it very difficult to predict who is going to be taken out next.

LINK: The latest victim was shot and killed on the 2nd of Octber in Bulwer – 45 year old Nkosinathi Ngocobo became the fifth ANC official to be gunned down in the Harry Gwala Region this year.

VO: Nkosinathi was gunned down on his way home.

While his family were still too traumatised to speak to us – his friend and fellow ANC member Xolani Zamisa showed us where Nkosinathi was killed.

XOLANI: I have not found comfort, I am not ok because I was very close to him.

VO: He says Nkosinathi feared for his life before he was killed.

XOLANI: On Saturday as well he spoke to me; saying that something was going to happen and we must watch each other’s backs-referring to me and him.
MAC: Do you think this had to do with his work.
XOLANI: This thing is about politics. // if you look at his death it’s the same way other comrades here in Harry Gwala have died, they were attacked and killed close to home.

VO: The KZN Provincial office is still not convinced that political motives are the driving force behind these murders.

NTULI: Our view as the ANC – we do not share the analogy that these are political killings, we believe that the inquiry, the work of law enforcement agencies need to be concluded before we can see without doubt that these are killings that are driven by political agendas

VO: Former KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu criticises the ANC’s apparent reluctance to acknowledge the political element.

SENZO: The ANC has to sit down and say there is a problem at home other wise there would be no smoke if there was no fire – you see the smoke and unfortunately in the form of dead bodies of our own comrades, our own people // INT1 M8

LINK: It all started in early 2016, when hitlist emerged with the names of ANC members linked to ousted KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu – some had been ticked off and others would follow.

NTULI: It is of deep concern for us. // it is not easy to lay our hands on the authors of the list – no one seems to know – except that it would be circulated through an sms from an unknown number

MARY: crime intelligence has been subverted to political ends – People know where to find hitmen and guns – ordinary people who order killings - why don’t the police know?

VO: And those links are crucial to solving these murders - because the reality is – hitmen don’t act alone, says Mchunu.

SENZO: There are people behind the trigger pullers for their own reasons – // we should trace it back to where they come from. And all of that needs effective policing.

VO: There has been more than one task team and even a commission which is currently under way… still the death toll continues to rise with very few arrests and even fewer convictions.

PROTAS: //You would think that these killing would go down while the Moerane Commission is running its course – but the killers are showing the commission the middle finger – we will kill despite because we know we will never be caught.

VO: When numerous requests for an interview with the HAWKS went unanswered, we got an insider’s perspective from a policeman working closely on these cases. Breaking rank, he asked that we hide his identity.

COP: the task team is established to work together // the way I look at it they not working together.

MARY: There’s no political will to address the shortcomings of the criminal justice system. You can’t say for certain it’s a political killing because you don’t get to who’s behind it.

COP: it’s Difficult the people are scared to give statements // They are scared for their life because when they hear that you give information they will kill you.

VO: De Haas says the fear in communities is palpable.

MARY: People don’t want to go to meetings at night – they are watching their backs // there’s a climate of fear out there.

PROTAS: It’s very well planned and they kill with military precision // they kill you on the spot.

VO: Everyone seems to be in agreement that the police have to up their game.

NTULI: The area we are not happy about as ANC – the capacity of The SAPS to gather info that can be used in a court of law – some cases people have been arrested – but no conviction - the reason is on the quality and credibility of evidence.

VO: Our police insider agrees – they just don’t have the capacity to get to the bottom of these killings.

COP: The investigators can do the work, the problem is the intelligence, the intelligence is not working at all // the investigators can not gather the information – they need intelligence to dig the information and produce it to the police - but they don’t. // Although I don’t know if there is people on top - they want the case not to be solved.

VO: But the family and friends of those murdered are desperate for answers.

XOLANI: Nothing happens but action is needed. They promise us that they will make arrests but nothing happens.
MAC: Are you worried about your safety?
XOLANI: I am not safe, I know that. Anything could happen.

VO: And until there is action from law enforcement agencies, the killings are likely continue.

MARY: // crime pays because they don’t get arrested, prosecuted or convicted – the crime carries on whether its political or not

VO: What’s happening in KZN is sadly not isolated.

SENZO: Crisis in the province reflects the crisis at a national level. Not united, not coherent

VO: This doesn’t bode well for the legitimacy of the ANC Conference at the end of the year says Madlala.

PROTAS: December is too far, I wonder when December comes how many lives we would have lost // There is this culture in KZN where a human life seems to be very cheap.


END

PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: The KZN political killings death toll is debatable. We ask what exactly is a political murder? And what is being done to stop this violent trend?


PROMO 2
VO: People are being gunned down in KZN – the motive is believed to be political – but is it that clear cut?

NTULI: Is this not what could be the attributes of a co-ordinated third force to disorganise us on a local government level.

PROMO 3
VO: A wave of alleged political killings has plagued KZN – a province awash with hitmen and guns for hire – the death toll continues to rise with very few arrests.

PROTAS: There is this culture in KZN where a human life seems to be very cheap.

Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 03 November 2017 Press Release: KZN Killing Fields Over the past few months, several people have been brutally gunned down in Kwazulu-Natal. At face value, the motives seem to be purely political, but is it that clear cut? Experts believe corruption, dodgy business deals and power struggles may well be behind some of the killings. Carte Blanche investigates Script: STRUCTURE VO: The province of KwaZulu Natal has been plagued by a wave of targeted assassinations believed to be political killings. More than 30 KZN ANC comrades have been murdered in just under two years across the province. LINK: The death toll is debatable. So are the motives. But what is fact is that people are being gunned down – people within the ANC. Is it a factionalism, a struggle for power or just corruption… VO: Politics and corruption go hand in hand – it’s a global trend says Political Analyst, Protas Madlala. PROTAS: You’ve never heard of someone being killed because that person was for corruption – it is always these people question, who are concerned about the looting of state resources or the monopoly of the access of state resources. VO: Violence Monitor Mary de Haas has been active in KZN since the eighties - she says the political dynamics in the province have changed - giving rise to political opportunism. MARY: What we have seen is deterioration of governance, an increase in corruption // together with corruption goes political competition over positions LINK: Being a mayor or a councillor is something many people would strive – but it’s become a dangerous job – one that some willing to literally kill for. PROTAS: It’s very easy to become a councillor you don’t need any formal qualification, you need to be a brave person, toy-toying and you buy a few members, local members to push up your name//the deal is once you are a councillor make sure those tenders come my ways – and anyone that stands in the way will have to be removed to the barrel of the gun VO: ANC KZN Provincial Spokesperson Mdumiseni Ntuli has a more sinister theory. NTULI: is it not part of what could be the attributes of a coordinated third force, who’s work is probably to disorganise us on a local government level and maybe even having the intentions of destabilising the provincial government. PROTAS: I don’t buy that crap. // we knew the third force in the 80s – the killings were state sponsored. Here – who is the third force? //if you know who the third force is go tell and the police. MAC: How is this different from what we saw 90s? MARY: The violence was widespread // it was not discriminatory – people were caught up in it because they lived in the wrong area – this is different – this is specifically targeting certain people for reasons // which may or may not be political and that makes it very difficult to predict who is going to be taken out next. LINK: The latest victim was shot and killed on the 2nd of Octber in Bulwer – 45 year old Nkosinathi Ngocobo became the fifth ANC official to be gunned down in the Harry Gwala Region this year. VO: Nkosinathi was gunned down on his way home. While his family were still too traumatised to speak to us – his friend and fellow ANC member Xolani Zamisa showed us where Nkosinathi was killed. XOLANI: I have not found comfort, I am not ok because I was very close to him. VO: He says Nkosinathi feared for his life before he was killed. XOLANI: On Saturday as well he spoke to me; saying that something was going to happen and we must watch each other’s backs-referring to me and him. MAC: Do you think this had to do with his work. XOLANI: This thing is about politics. // if you look at his death it’s the same way other comrades here in Harry Gwala have died, they were attacked and killed close to home. VO: The KZN Provincial office is still not convinced that political motives are the driving force behind these murders. NTULI: Our view as the ANC – we do not share the analogy that these are political killings, we believe that the inquiry, the work of law enforcement agencies need to be concluded before we can see without doubt that these are killings that are driven by political agendas VO: Former KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu criticises the ANC’s apparent reluctance to acknowledge the political element. SENZO: The ANC has to sit down and say there is a problem at home other wise there would be no smoke if there was no fire – you see the smoke and unfortunately in the form of dead bodies of our own comrades, our own people // INT1 M8 LINK: It all started in early 2016, when hitlist emerged with the names of ANC members linked to ousted KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu – some had been ticked off and others would follow. NTULI: It is of deep concern for us. // it is not easy to lay our hands on the authors of the list – no one seems to know – except that it would be circulated through an sms from an unknown number MARY: crime intelligence has been subverted to political ends – People know where to find hitmen and guns – ordinary people who order killings - why don’t the police know? VO: And those links are crucial to solving these murders - because the reality is – hitmen don’t act alone, says Mchunu. SENZO: There are people behind the trigger pullers for their own reasons – // we should trace it back to where they come from. And all of that needs effective policing. VO: There has been more than one task team and even a commission which is currently under way… still the death toll continues to rise with very few arrests and even fewer convictions. PROTAS: //You would think that these killing would go down while the Moerane Commission is running its course – but the killers are showing the commission the middle finger – we will kill despite because we know we will never be caught. VO: When numerous requests for an interview with the HAWKS went unanswered, we got an insider’s perspective from a policeman working closely on these cases. Breaking rank, he asked that we hide his identity. COP: the task team is established to work together // the way I look at it they not working together. MARY: There’s no political will to address the shortcomings of the criminal justice system. You can’t say for certain it’s a political killing because you don’t get to who’s behind it. COP: it’s Difficult the people are scared to give statements // They are scared for their life because when they hear that you give information they will kill you. VO: De Haas says the fear in communities is palpable. MARY: People don’t want to go to meetings at night – they are watching their backs // there’s a climate of fear out there. PROTAS: It’s very well planned and they kill with military precision // they kill you on the spot. VO: Everyone seems to be in agreement that the police have to up their game. NTULI: The area we are not happy about as ANC – the capacity of The SAPS to gather info that can be used in a court of law – some cases people have been arrested – but no conviction - the reason is on the quality and credibility of evidence. VO: Our police insider agrees – they just don’t have the capacity to get to the bottom of these killings. COP: The investigators can do the work, the problem is the intelligence, the intelligence is not working at all // the investigators can not gather the information – they need intelligence to dig the information and produce it to the police - but they don’t. // Although I don’t know if there is people on top - they want the case not to be solved. VO: But the family and friends of those murdered are desperate for answers. XOLANI: Nothing happens but action is needed. They promise us that they will make arrests but nothing happens. MAC: Are you worried about your safety? XOLANI: I am not safe, I know that. Anything could happen. VO: And until there is action from law enforcement agencies, the killings are likely continue. MARY: // crime pays because they don’t get arrested, prosecuted or convicted – the crime carries on whether its political or not VO: What’s happening in KZN is sadly not isolated. SENZO: Crisis in the province reflects the crisis at a national level. Not united, not coherent VO: This doesn’t bode well for the legitimacy of the ANC Conference at the end of the year says Madlala. PROTAS: December is too far, I wonder when December comes how many lives we would have lost // There is this culture in KZN where a human life seems to be very cheap. END PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: The KZN political killings death toll is debatable. We ask what exactly is a political murder? And what is being done to stop this violent trend? PROMO 2 VO: People are being gunned down in KZN – the motive is believed to be political – but is it that clear cut? NTULI: Is this not what could be the attributes of a co-ordinated third force to disorganise us on a local government level. PROMO 3 VO: A wave of alleged political killings has plagued KZN – a province awash with hitmen and guns for hire – the death toll continues to rise with very few arrests. PROTAS: There is this culture in KZN where a human life seems to be very cheap.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: PEOPLE ARE BEING KILLED IN KZN – THE MOTIVE IS SAID TO BE POLITICAL. IT’S A STORY THAT WE HAVE NOT COVERED, BUT IT’S NOT GOING AWAY. IT’S CONTROVERSIAL BECAUSE OF DIFFERENT VIEWS ABOUT WHAT THE REAL REASON IS BEHIND THE APPARENT KILLING SPREE.
metadata.Summary: Political killings in KZN have intensified within the alliance during the post-Polokwane period. Same the there is a sinister third force at play while other point to an internal struggle for power, positions and access to resources. The death toll differs according to different soures. We ask what exactly is a political murder? And what is being done to stop this violent trend?
metadata.Further information: THE STATUS QUO It appears that there is a glaring lack of political will to find out, exactly, who is being killed for political purposes, and how to prevent this from happening again. Political murders need, by their nature, political intervention. They are, after all, not so much capital crimes as they are indicators that something is deeply dysfunctional in our politics. But despite the highly-publicised task teams, there is no indication that they are being treated as anything else but ordinary crimes. THE TASK TEAMS THAT HAVE YET TO DELIVER Before the 2016 Local Government Elections, there was a spate of murders. So many, in fact, that the KZN provincial ANC called for a special task team to investigate them. The Hawks had already formulated a task team to deal with political murders, and the national ANC had called for an internal investigation into why the victims were, almost exclusively, ANC members. In fact, as far back as 2011, Police Commissioner Bheki Cele had established an SAPS task team. But none of these four so-called task teams have actually come up with any results, other than ordinary policing. THE MOERANE COMMISSION OF INQUIRY KZN Premier Willies Mchunu established the commission in October 2016, chaired by advocate Marumo Moerane, to investigate the high number of political killings in the province since 2011. The hearings are currently under way. ANC VIEWS The ANC in KwaZulu-Natal believes the killing of its public representatives could be the result of “sponsored violence” similar to that experienced in the 1980s. ANC provincial secretary Super Zuma said the violence could be meant to use KwaZulu-Natal as an “entry point” towards destabilising the country. Zuma said the ANC was not conclusively saying there is a third force element at work, but wants that aspect to be investigated. He said with the recent killings there were patterns which mirrored those of the violence of the 1980s. “It is not just violence, these are assassinations by well trained people,” he said. JULY 2017: spokesperson for the ANC in KwaZulu-Natal, Mdumiseni Ntuli, has dismissed claims that the recent killings are politically motivated. The ANC’s Ntuli said: “We cannot confirm that the violence is politically motivated and I urge people to stay away from these baseless assumptions. This issue is not that straightforward. There is no clear political motivation. Therefore, to say that the incident is politically motivated is a very dangerous assumption.” CRITICISM FROM WITHIN THE ANC RANKS Former KZN Premier Senzo Mchunu says the organisation must take responsibility for its contribution to the killings in the province & the ANC will need strong leadership that does not rely on factions to survive. Mchunu said the reason corruption had become so rampant in both the public and the private sector was due to the lack of principled individuals. "You can’t just be corrupt in an island [sic]. You need people to assist you, you co-opt them, then you become the chief corruptor, they become assistant corruptors." He says corruption within the ANC is partly to blame for the divisions plaguing the party. "Jellyfish who feel bound to support a corrupt person or corrupt individuals and they become one club. So people get divided not because there is hatred among them, but just because you are defending that side and defending this thing that we should not be defending." He’s warned corruption factionalism and the manipulation of party lists has put the ANC at the centre of political killings. Mchunu says corruption breeds hatred within the organisation and warned that the manipulation of ANC processes has contributed to the increase in political murders in the province. Mchunu says weak internal ANC systems and corruption have linked the party to political murders. “People are always going to compete but make it clean so that competing for positions via manipulation doesn’t yield benefits for anyone.” VIOLENCE MONITORS VIEWS Violence monitor Mary De Haas She said most killings in the province are linked to factions and power struggles in the ANC. “The worst problem is a lack of political will to investigate these murders,” says violence monitor Mary de Haas. “There is no lack of people willing to testify, but no one is joining the dots. And no one is asking the hard questions about where the ultimate culpability lies.” She might be a better bet – long history violence monitoring – can give interesting comparitive views and experienced insights. INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES Lizette Lancaster, a researcher, said political killings could not be looked at in isolation from how SA has generally dealt with conflict. “There is clearly a culture among some people to get rid of opponents, often for political reasons. All our research shows that in terms of just general political violence there are often hotspots, a type of modus operandi, whether it is political conflict, strike action or vigilantism,” she said. Looking at the political killings in KZN, Lancaster said with good crime intelligence it was difficult to comprehend how the role players are not known by law enforcement. WHAT IS BEING DONE? POLICE Police Minister Fikile Mbalula said he was beefing up the extraordinary measures already put in place to deal with the violence. An integrated provincial project task team consisting of the Hawks, the detective service, crime intelligence, the local criminal records centre and the National Prosecuting Authority was announced by Mbalula in May to deal with political killings. Members of the Public Order Policing Unit, the Tactical Response Team, the National Intervention Unit and Visible Policing were also deployed in some of the hotspots. Despite this, the killings have continued. The task team investigating political murders in the province has registered 42 cases, 24 of which are murder cases. Almost 35 suspects have been arrested in 10 murder cases, he said. According to Mulaudzi, almost 24 cases are still under investigation and 28 firearms have been seized. In September, the Hawks have offered a R450,000 reward for any information that could lead to the arrest of suspects in the ongoing political killings in KwaZulu-Natal. CRITICISM FOR THE POLICE Former KZN premier Mchunu says the use of state security organs for political ends is a betrayal of what they fought against during apartheid. Mchunu says there's an urgent need to restore confidence in the police. “Failure to arrest, it scarps confidence, that’s the consequence, that is where we might be heading if nothing is done to actually make police fire on all engines to ensure necessary confidence in the police, and everybody’s confidence.” Violence monitor Vanessa Burger (VERY CONTROVERSIAL IN KZN) she accused IPID of having failed to investigate allegations of police misconduct and brutality at Glebelands Hostel in Umlazi. IPID responded asking her sto substantiate claims – back & forth … would rather avoid her. WHAT IS A POLITICAL MURDER? Press define a political murder as a killing where the victim had been a political office-bearer, or the motive was linked to their political affiliation. This was far too superficial. While there were murders where the victim had clearly been blocking someone’s political path. Most of the murders appeared to be business deals gone sour, whistle-blowers getting removed, an overspill from taxi wars, family feuds, revenge killings, thieves falling out, personal disputes and in some cases the wrong person was killed by mistake. DEATH TOLL The figure is debatable…. Some say 60 people were gunned down in suspected political assassinations in KwaZulu-Natal between April 2014 and August 2016. In June, on an official visit to KwaZulu-Natal last month, police minister Fikile Mbalula said that 33 political killings that had taken place in the province since January 2016 were being investigated. RECENT CASES: JULY 2017: Former ANC Youth League secretary general Sindiso Magaqa, now a councillor, and two other ward councillors, Nontsikelelo Mafa and Jabu Mzizi, were attacked by unknown gunmen. All three are in hospital in critical condition. This attack follows three murders in Umzimkhulu this year. Khaya Thobela, the ANC’s regional deputy secretary and Umzimkhulu’s municipal speaker, died after being shot in April. Khayelihle Mgcwaba, a former ward councillor and a political activist, was murdered in mid-May. A few weeks later, Mduduzi Tshivase, a councillor in Harry Gwala district, was gunned down. MOST RECENT MURDER 30 / 31 AUGUST 2017 African National Congress (ANC) ward 3 councillor Kwazi Mkhize, 34, of the uMkhambathini Local Municipality in the Midlands, was gunned down by an unknown assailant outside the Nkanyezini Community Hall. He had concluded an extended branch executive committee meeting, where he was reporting on development projects in his ward. According to the ANC in KZN, Mkhize and his siblings were allegedly closing the gate of the community hall when he was killed. "Although details regarding Cde Mkhize’s murder remain sketchy, it appears his attacker fired from behind and killed him on the scene." RESEARCH Jouranlist Niki Moore compliped a list of “political murders” over the last 18 months, arranged according to the apparent picture of motive for The Daily Maverick. See has doen extensive research showing that there are overlaps and contradictions, but one thing is clear: the endgame is all about power and money.
